node_modules/react-chatbot-kit v2.2.2 package.json: main=build/index.js (CJS, no module/exports fields). build/index.js ends with `e.r(t),e.d(t,{Chatbot:()=>B,createChatBotMessage:..,default:()=>H,useChatbot:..}); ... H=B; module.exports=t`, and e.r sets __esModule=true. So module.exports is a namespace with getters Chatbot=B and default=H=B (same component). Interop cases: (1) babel/webpack/esModuleInterop honor __esModule so default import = t.default = B; B.Chatbot is undefined so `?? chatbotKit` yields B. (2) Vite/Node ESM map default to module.exports = t; t.Chatbot = B, unwrapped. Either way the result is B. Absolute-claim input considered: a bundler that sets default to module.exports despite __esModule (case 2) - handled by .Chatbot; getters are enumerable-defined on the object so property access works. Did not execute under each bundler; established by reading the build file.

node_modules/react-chatbot-kit/build/index.js (v2.2.2, package.json main=build/index.js) is a webpack 5 bundle. Exports are defined via e.d(t,{Chatbot:()=>B,...,default:()=>H,...}), which uses Object.defineProperty with get: getters, so a static named-export lexer cannot see them. e.r(t) sets __esModule=true. The bundle ends with H=B;module.exports=t. So under webpack/babel interop, __esModule makes the default import t.default = H = B, the Chatbot class. Under Vite/Node ESM, default maps to module.exports, which is the namespace object t. That matches the comment at src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:32-35, and the unwrap at line 36 handles both cases.

ChatWidget.tsx:228-234 keepInsideViewport sets maxWidth from window.innerWidth and calls clampPosition(prev, dimensions). clampPosition (116-122) uses viewport() (101-104), which reads only window.innerWidth/innerHeight. A grep for visualViewport in src finds only the listener registration at ChatWidget.tsx:242-243 (plus tests); visualViewport.width/height is never read. So a visualViewport resize that leaves innerWidth/innerHeight unchanged produces the same maxWidth (the guard returns prev) and the same clamped position (setPosition returns prev when x and y are equal), so nothing changes. Input: open the floating window in a viewport shorter than MIN_HEIGHT (400, e.g. a landscape phone about 360px tall) or narrower than MIN_WIDTH (300). The open effect (ChatWidget.tsx:254-256) calls keepInsideViewport, which calls clampPosition (116-122). That sets x = max(0, min(x, vw - width)) and y likewise, so it floors at 0 when the window is larger than the viewport. It never shrinks the window. windowStyle (519-538) sets minWidth/minHeight to 300/400 px. In CSS, min-* overrides both max-width: 100% and max-height: min(..., 100%). The window therefore stays 400px tall in a 360px viewport, with top at 0 and its bottom 40px offscreen. Narrow viewports overflow to the right in the same way. Re-clamping on open does not guarantee the window never appears offscreen, so the comment at line 253 is wrong for this case. The position clamp does handle restored dimensions larger than the viewport, because max-width/max-height 100% shrink the window.

ChatWidget.tsx:228-234 keepInsideViewport is useCallback with [dimensions], so identity changes on every setDimensions, including each useResize mousemove (ResizeHandles.tsx:95-103). The effect at ChatWidget.tsx:254-256 therefore re-runs mid-gesture. For left/top resize, computeResize (ResizeHandles.tsx:71-78) sets x = startLeft-(width-startWidth), so x+width = startLeft+startWidth (the original right edge, already in viewport) and y+height likewise. clampPosition (ChatWidget.tsx:116-122) clamps x to [0, vw-width] and y to [0, vh-height], which is a no-op for those values (computeResize also floors x,y at 0 and width <= maxWidth = viewport width). The setPosition functional updater returns prev when unchanged, and the next mousemove recomputes from the gesture's start values, so any clamp is overwritten anyway; the maxWidth sync only re-subscribes the listener effect, and the gesture keeps its start values. No disagreement for left/top. Caveat (not a defect against any source): for right/bottom drags, useResize never sets position, so once x+width exceeds the viewport the clamp slides x left, pinning the far edge to the viewport rather than letting the window overflow.

ChatWidget.tsx:531-537 sets minWidth 300px / minHeight 400px (MIN_WIDTH/MIN_HEIGHT at lines 62-63, 203-204) in the same style object as maxWidth '100%' and maxHeight min(Npx,100%). In CSS, min-width/min-height override max-width/max-height, so for a viewport narrower than 300px or shorter than 400px (e.g. a landscape phone ~360px tall, or a 280px-wide viewport) the fixed window is 300x400 and outgrows the viewport. The 'never outgrow' claim and comment are false in that case. Normal viewports are fitted.

ChatWidget.tsx:526,534-537 sets position:fixed with maxWidth:'100%' / maxHeight:min(..,100%) and comments that the fixed containing block is the viewport. mount() (mount.tsx:18,24) does createRoot(element) on any host-chosen element; there is no portal to document.body and no shadow root. chat.css:69-74 (.radchat-widget) and the .radchat-container rules (146-158) set no transform/contain to reset ancestors.
